CDMX Food Itinerary

A group of five eating through Mexico City — tamales at dawn, a Coyoacán paella, a late-night Centro taco crawl, and one Yucatecan lunch in Cancún to finish.

Sunday, Oct 18

Roma Sur → Coyoacán → Centro — 8 stops, ending in a night crawl

Order this

  • Verde con puerco, mole con puerco, and rajas
  • The signatures: huitlacoche con queso de cabra, and frijol con queso y chapulines
  • Sweet: higo con queso
  • A guajolota — a tamal tucked into a bolillo — with champurrado, reputedly the city's best

Good to know: Morning-only (Sat–Sun 8:30–14:30) and closed Mondays. Arrive early — popular flavors sell out. About $55 MXN a piece; a ~7-minute walk from base.

Jalapa esq. Tlaxcala, Roma Sur · Open in Maps

Add to Google Calendar

Order this

  • Traditional pan de muerto — the loaf to judge everything else against

On the group's actual criterion — softest crumb — Forte has the strongest claim in the city: Chilango's judged tasting of 18 bakeries crowned Forte's traditional loaf and singled out its exceptional softness.

Good to know: Forte's Sunday hours and 2026 price weren't confirmed — check before walking over. Backup: Costra (Av. Universidad 482, Narvarte), traditional soft crumb at $55, sells out early.

Querétaro 116, Roma Norte · Open in Maps

Add to Google Calendar

Order this

  • Aguachile negro de camarón — the dish they're famous for
  • Ceviche tripón — the best straight ceviche of the trip
  • La Señora Torres, the seafood tower built for five
  • Costra de camarón

Good to know: Sinaloa-style mariscos, open Tue–Sun 12:00–20:00 (closed Mondays). Reservations are murky — the safe play is to be there at the 12:00 opening. Bonus nearby: Mercado Coyoacán's tamales de elote from the stand on Calle Xicoténcatl, before ~13:00.

Felipe Carrillo Puerto esq. Venustiano Carranza, Coyoacán · Open in Maps

Add to Google Calendar

Order this

  • Mixed paella (mar, tierra y huerto) — the centerpiece
  • Tortilla española, patatas bravas, croquetas de jamón Jabugo
  • Calamares a la romana, chistorra con queso
  • The famous tortas (Del Mar, Gallega) if anyone's still pacing themselves
  • Torrijas for dessert; sangría or the house beer, Espantapájaros

Good to know: Coyoacán's Spanish house since 1988 — press calls its paella one of the best in Mexico City. Sunday hours 13:00–20:30, about 5 minutes from Mi Compa Chava. The rice is cooked to order, so put the paella order in first — and plan to leave Coyoacán by ~15:30 for the afternoon.

Av. Centenario 91-C, Coyoacán · Open in Maps

Add to Google Calendar

Order this

  • Plato de birria de res con su consomé
  • Tacos de birria, and a quesabirria
  • Taco de espinazo for round two

Good to know: Mexico City's most famous birria house, going since 1934 — but note the style: birria de res tatemada (seared beef), not goat. Open daily 8:00–1:00. It's a loud working cantina; mariachis charge per song.

Worth knowing: La Polar closed for several months in 2023 after a diner died in an altercation with staff. It reopened in August 2023 and has operated normally since — the group's call.

Guillermo Prieto 129, San Rafael · Open in Maps

Add to Google Calendar

Order this

  • Tacos al pastor — several each
  • Volcán al pastor
  • Cazuela de queso
  • Agua de horchata

Good to know: This is the 1959 original, and a deliberate outlier — their pastor comes with no pineapple and no cilantro, just trompo meat, onion and salsas. Walk-in only; expect a queue. Want the classic style with piña instead? El Tizoncito (Tamaulipas 122, Condesa) is 5 minutes from base and open until 3:30 AM; the canonical old-school challenger is Los Güeros de Boturini (Lorenzo Boturini 4354, Sundays until 01:00), a detour east.

Ayuntamiento 21, Centro · Open in Maps

Add to Google Calendar

Order this

  • Suadero — best late, after hours braising in the cauldron (Michelin's tip)
  • Tripa, bien doradita (well crisped)
  • Lengua — called the best in Mexico City
  • Cabeza / cachete, and a campechano
  • Sesos or ojo, for the adventurous

Good to know: Cash only — bring bills. Open 24/7; a Michelin Bib Gourmand and a Bourdain institution, about 10 minutes from El Huequito. Orders of three run ~$70 MXN for lengua, suadero or tripa. Buche isn't on the published menu — ask at the counter, don't count on it.

Simón Bolívar 59, Centro · Open in Maps

Add to Google Calendar

Order this

  • Classic cinnamon-sugar churros
  • Two chocolates for the table — Mexicano (the lightest) and Español (the thickest) — and compare
  • Consuelitos (ice-cream-filled) and a cajeta dip, if there's room

Good to know: The 1935 original, open 24 hours — the Centro location is the experience; skip the Roma/Condesa branches. Go at a busy hour so they're frying fresh.

Monday, Oct 19

Pyramids by day — a Condesa dinner to close

Order this

  • Verde, mole, and rajas
  • Oaxaqueño-style
  • Champurrado

Good to know: From $22 MXN a piece. Roundups list a Monday opening around 9:00–16:00 and times conflict slightly — so treat this one as tentative and go only if the tour pickup allows. Doña Emi is closed Mondays, which is why this is the Monday pick.

Chihuahua 1 Local B, Roma Norte · Open in Maps

Add to Google Calendar

Order this

  • The seasonal tasting menu, ~$900–1,000 MXN per person, or
  • À la carte, ~$500–700 per person without drinks

Good to know: The table for five is already reserved — just be on time. Chef Víctor Toriz (Bestia LA, Arca Tulum); the restaurant is a Michelin Guide 2026 debut, about 10 minutes from base.

Av. Mazatlán 190, Hipódromo Condesa · Open in Maps

Tuesday, Oct 20

Tolantongo day trip — via Real del Monte on the way out

Order this

  • Papa con carne — the classic paste, the Cornish-pasty descendant brought by English miners
  • Also try mole and tinga fillings
  • Hot chocolate to go with them — it is cold up here in the morning
  • Grab a box for the car if the counter is moving fast

Real del Monte is a Pueblo Mágico English-mining town on the Mex 105 mountain corridor — the outbound route to Tolantongo that morning, after the ~06:00 departure from CDMX. Pastes El Portal, on the main portal, opens early (from ~7:00–8:00), so an 08:00 stop works.

Good to know: The town's sights — Museo del Paste and the Panteón Inglés — open at 9:00, so they're only for a linger, not this quick stop. Bring a layer: it's cold up there. From Real del Monte it's ~2 hrs onward to Tolantongo (park arrival ~10:45). The return drive that night goes via the Mex 85 highway (Actopan / Ixmiquilpan), not back over the mountain road — fog.

Portal del Comercio 2, Mineral del Monte, Hidalgo · Open in Maps

Add to Google Calendar
At Tolantongo itself: Inside the Tolantongo park it's cash-only food stalls — quesadillas and the like — and there are no ATMs, so carry roughly $350–500 MXN per person in cash (park entry is $230 per person). The group leaves Roma early (~06:00) and heads back by ~17:00 for the daylight canyon descent.

Wednesday, Oct 21

Cancún — one last lunch

Order this

  • Sopa de lima first — it's the reviewed specialty
  • Cochinita pibil, as tacos or panuchos
  • Panuchos, salbutes, queso relleno, papadzules
  • Agua de piña con chaya

Good to know: A Yucatecan lonchería open since 1988, hours 8:00–20:00 — go for lunch after check-in. Skip the old guidebook names: Labná is permanently closed, and sources contradict each other on whether La Habichuela's downtown original is open, so it's unusable for planning.

Calle 31 Norte, Lote 23, Mz 35, SM 63, Centro, Cancún · Open in Maps

About this plan

Every pick was verified on Oct 16–17, 2026 — address, hours for the specific day, and signature order — from official listings, local press and Google. Prices are restaurant prices in MXN and can move. Two honest caveats stay open: Forte's Sunday hours and 2026 price, and Tamalito Corazón's exact Monday opening time, couldn't be confirmed — both are flagged on their cards.
